Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Patient Age: 45 years
Gender: Male
Date of admission: [REDACTED]
Date of discharge: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with symptoms of intermittent fever, chills and rigors along with night sweats, loss of appetite, and weight loss. The patient also had a transient macular rash and generalized painful lymphadenopathy. Synovitis involving lower limb small joints was noted following the presentation that progressed to larger joints in the lower and upper limbs. Laboratory investigations revealed high white cell counts, normocytic anemia and high inflammatory markers which were in a rising trend following the onset of arthritis. The patient was diagnosed as a case of DLBCL following a lymph node biopsy.

Treatment:
The patient was started on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents and colchicine for the arthritis but there was no response to treatment. Treatment with RCHOP chemotherapy commenced which showed a marked response in the synovitis following the first cycle of therapy. The patient completed the chemotherapy with intermittent infections.

Summary:
The patient presented with symptoms of intermittent fever, chills, and rigors along with night sweats, loss of appetite, and weight loss. The patient had synovitis involving the small and large joints of the upper and lower limbs with a lower limb predominance. Laboratory investigations revealed high white cell counts and anemia. A lymph node biopsy was positive for DLBCL. The patient underwent RCHOP chemotherapy which resulted in the complete resolution of synovitis. The patient was discharged in stable condition with a follow-up plan for further evaluation and management.

text:
# Principal Diagnosis: **C83.3 – Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma**

## Rationale

**Why DLBCL is the principal diagnosis**
- Under ACS 0001 (Principal Diagnosis), the principal diagnosis is the condition established after study to be chiefly responsible for the admission.
- The presenting features were B symptoms (fever, rigors, night sweats, weight loss), lymphadenopathy, rash and polyarthritis. All were ultimately explained by DLBCL, confirmed on lymph node biopsy.
- Under ACS 0002, symptoms and signs integral to a confirmed diagnosis are not coded as the principal diagnosis.
- The DLBCL was also the focus of definitive treatment (R-CHOP) during the admission.

**Why not Z51.1 (chemotherapy session)?**
- Z51.1 is used when the patient is admitted specifically for chemotherapy, such as a same-day admission.
- Here the patient was admitted with undiagnosed symptoms, worked up and diagnosed during the stay. The neoplasm is therefore principal.

## Suggested Additional Codes

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| **M36.1*** | Arthropathy in neoplastic disease (paraneoplastic synovitis). This is an asterisk code paired with **C83.3†** under dagger/asterisk convention. |
| **D63.0*** | Anaemia in neoplastic disease, if it meets ACS 0002 additional diagnosis criteria. |
| Infection codes | Code according to the documented organism or site, with **Y43.3** (adverse effect of antineoplastic drugs) and **D70.1** if drug-induced neutropenia is documented. |
| **Morphology code** | **M9680/3** (Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS). |
| **ACHI intervention codes** | Lymph node biopsy and chemotherapy administration (e.g., 96199-00 [1920] intravenous administration of antineoplastic agent). |

*Final code assignment should be confirmed against the specific ICD-10-AM edition and Australian Coding Standards in use at your facility.*
